rationale.complete: Round 1 done: card, impostor table and dated predictions before real data; synthetic validation at the real unit layout (found the design SE 2.5x optimistic and adopted the powered ratio form before real data); 71-unit replication with sensitivities (WLS, roster N, span N, active hours, within-regime); three natives (NE42, G51 sweep, G38 room contrast plus three more rooms-era periods); post hoc decomposition; scorecard; frozen, guarded confirm script dry-run, not run. Per-unit rows in per_period_estimates. No holdout run; no within-agent work design.
rationale.faithfulness: The consistency check of H18's dilution passes for addressing per message (0.79 [0.41, 1.39] vs 0.44 predicted from the measured k scaling) and fails for reply parents (kill fires). The extensive-talk premise fails: messages scale as N^0.33, with a nearly fixed room talk volume in regime I. Both natives that would intervene on N failed or were unidentified, and work exponents are unidentified. Scorecard A1 B1 C1 D1 E0 F2 G1 H1 I1.
rationale.usefulness: Tells an operator that adding agents does not add talk (regime I room talk volume ~130/h from 4 to 11 agents; per-agent talk share falls as N^-0.89), that addressing per message grows with room size, and that cross-period output exponents carry +-0.5 uncertainty. Does not yet say whether more agents produce more work.

one_line: Talk scales sublinearly with N (messages N^0.33; regime I room talk nearly fixed); addressing per message rises as H18's dilution predicts (0.79 vs 0.44); reply parents do not aggregate; work exponents unidentified.

models.note: Talk sublinear (0.33); addressing per message aggregates; work unidentified
Per-call dilution aggregates for addressing, not for reply parents

v2.claim: Talk scales sublinearly with N (β_msg 0.33; regime-I talk volume nearly conserved), while addressing per message rises with N (slope 0.79), consistent with H18's dilution; reply volume does not follow the predicted N^1.34; work exponents are not identifiable at 71 units
v2.scope: 71 units, 35 goal clusters; natives NE42, G51, G38

ladder.factor: synthetic identification (primary moved to the per-message slope before real data)

v2.decision: plan talk budgets: adding agents does not add proportional talk
v2.rater: 2 raters (coordinator + blind); log-odds mean; ADJUDICATION NEEDED

raters.claim: Across non-holdout period units with regime intercepts, room message volume per scheduled hour grows sublinearly with active population (beta_msg 0.33 [-0.18, 0.64]; ~0.09 in regime I), i.e. not as an independent-agent sum. Excluded: the addressing-slope pass (P3; two thirds is post hoc co-addressing), reply aggregation (kill fired), work and repo exponents (unidentified), NE42/G51 natives.
ladder: calibrated estimator (synthetic at the real 71-unit layout: bias <=0.02, cluster-CI coverage 0.90-0.93, regime-confound scenario)
partial replication (within-day room-size contrasts in 4 rooms-era periods: same sign, RE 0.85 [0.17, 1.53]; G38 0.36)
partly robust (WLS, roster N, span N, active hours: 0.26-0.52)
known confound: N grew with calendar time (model generations, operator practice) and regime-I chat mode capped the visible window; regime III is near-extensive (0.77)
